2_Introduction: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 9.51%, with a VOC of 0.89 V, FF of 51.53%, and JSC of 20.66 mA/cm². The composition of the 1.73 mol/L perovskite film is Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1. The perovskite solution was spin-coated in two steps, namely 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 6 s before the end of the program. After the spin coating was completed, it was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. Image analysis shows that the spin-coating coverage reaches 99.5%, and the average grayscale value of the film is 9.2777. Spectral analysis indicates that, upon the onset of annealing, the film reaches the explosive nucleation point at 6.8 seconds, at which the photoluminescence (PL) intensity attains its maximum. Following this peak, the PL intensity decreases to 30% of its maximum value, with an average decay slope of 2.263482232.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation mixed-halide perovskite Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1, formulated at a high precursor concentration of 1.73 mol/L, benefits from a favorable tolerance factor that enhances phase stability, while the optimized two-step spin-coating process (1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s) with chlorobenzene antisolvent dripping at 6 s before the end precisely controls solvent evaporation and supersaturation, directing crystallization kinetics. The incorporated additives collectively modulate this process; one additive governs the formation of intermediate phases and suppresses premature nucleation, while another selectively passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ defects at grain boundaries and the perovskite surface, with their synergistic interaction ensuring a dense, pinhole-minimized morphology as directly evidenced by image analysis showing exceptional 99.5% film coverage and a highly uniform average grayscale value of 9.2777. This morphological control is corroborated by in-situ photoluminescence spectral analysis, where the explosive nucleation event at 6.8 seconds into the 110°C annealing step—marked by the PL intensity maximum—followed by a rapid decay to 30% of the peak value with an average slope of 2.263482232, signifies fast, directed crystalline growth and a reduction in non-radiative recombination centers, ultimately leading to improved charge extraction. The concerted action of the additives in managing crystallization dynamics and passivating ionic defects thus enhances interfacial charge transport, yielding a power conversion efficiency of 9.51% with an open-circuit voltage of 0.89 V, a short-circuit current density of 20.66 mA/cm², and a fill factor of 51.53%.
